source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public Job 1–26 binds all 612 matching original Hebrew records, including all source notes. Chapters 27–42 remain outside this draft batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the fourfold ethical description without claiming sinless perfection.
verses.before: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.
verses.after: There was a man in the land of Uz named Job. He was a man of integrity, upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.

verses.rationale: Preserve the exact numbers and specified genders.
verses.before: Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
verses.after: He had seven sons and three daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

verses.rationale: Keep all livestock counts, paired oxen, female donkeys, and regional distinction.
verses.before: His possessions were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very large household. That man was greater than all the people of the east.
verses.after: He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys, with a very large household workforce. He was the greatest of all the people of the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: His possessions were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and a very large household. That man was greater than all the people of the east.

verses.rationale: Leave each son’s day unspecified rather than asserting birthdays.
verses.before: His sons would go and hold a feast in the house of each person on his day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
verses.after: His sons would take turns holding banquets in their homes, each on his own day. They would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: His sons would go and hold a feast in the house of each one on his day, and they would send and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

verses.rationale: Preserve precautionary rather than proven guilt; render the blessing euphemism contextually.
verses.before: When the days of feasting had completed their cycle, Job would send and consecrate them. He would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus Job did continually.
verses.after: When a round of banquets was over, Job would send for them and consecrate them. He rose early in the morning and offered burnt offerings for each of them, thinking, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Job did this regularly.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the days of feasting had completed their cycle, Job would send and consecrate them. He would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus Job did continually.

verses.rationale: Retain the divine-council designation and the accuser’s title rather than assuming a personal name.
verses.before: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser also came among them.
verses.after: One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser came among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser also came among them.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated movement and direct exchange.
verses.before: The LORD said to the accuser, “From where have you come?” The accuser answered the LORD and said, “From roaming through the earth and walking about on it.”
verses.after: The LORD asked the accuser, “Where have you come from?” The accuser answered, “From roaming the earth and walking about on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the accuser, “From where have you come?” The accuser answered the LORD and said, “From roaming through the earth and walking about on it.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the narrator’s fourfold description in the LORD’s appraisal.
verses.before: The LORD said to the accuser, “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil.”
verses.after: The LORD said to the accuser, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: a man of integrity, upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the accuser, “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the question about disinterested reverence, echoed by without cause in 2:3.
verses.before: Then the accuser answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
verses.after: The accuser answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the accuser answered the LORD and said, “Does Job fear God for nothing?

verses.rationale: Keep the protective hedge and expanding livestock images.
verses.before: Have you not put a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have spread throughout the land.
verses.after: Have you not put a hedge around him, his household, and everything he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have spread across the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you not put a hedge around him, around his household, and around all that he has on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have spread throughout the land.

verses.rationale: Retain the hand and face imagery and contextual curse euphemism.
verses.before: But now stretch out your hand and touch all that he has. Surely he will curse you to your face.”
verses.after: But stretch out your hand and touch everything he has. He will surely curse you to your face!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But now stretch out your hand and touch all that he has. Surely he will curse you to your face.”

verses.rationale: Preserve permission and its explicit bodily limit without softening agency.

verses.after: The LORD said to the accuser, “Everything he has is in your hands. But do not lay a hand on the man himself.” Then the accuser left the LORD’s presence.

verses.rationale: Keep both sons and daughters and the precise gathering place.

verses.after: One day Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was a day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother.

verses.rationale: Begin the report before the calamity, preserving the ordinary work scene.
verses.before: A messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were feeding beside them,
verses.after: A messenger came to Job and said, “The oxen were plowing and the female donkeys were grazing nearby,

verses.rationale: Keep human deaths and the survivor refrain alongside property loss.
verses.before: and the Sabeans fell upon them and took them, and struck the servants with the edge of the sword. I alone escaped to tell you.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the messenger’s attribution of the fire, not a new narrator explanation.

verses.after: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Fire from God fell from heaven, burning up the sheep and the workers. I alone escaped to tell you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: While this one was still speaking, another came and said, “The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them. I alone escaped to tell you.”

verses.rationale: Retain the three bands and repeated deaths and survivor formula.
verses.before: While this one was still speaking, another came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three companies, raided the camels, and took them, and struck the servants with the edge of the sword. I alone escaped to tell you.”
verses.after: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three raiding bands, swept down on the camels, and carried them off. They killed the workers with the sword. I alone escaped to tell you.”

verses.rationale: Repeat the opening domestic scene as the fourth report begins.
verses.before: While this one was still speaking, another came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
verses.after: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
verses.tsw_comparator: While this one was still speaking, another came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,

verses.rationale: Render the collective youths to include the daughters and preserve all four corners.
verses.before: and look, a great wind came from beyond the wilderness, struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people, and they died. I alone escaped to tell you.”
verses.after: when a great wind came across the wilderness and struck the house’s four corners. It collapsed on the young people, and they died. I alone escaped to tell you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and look, a great wind came from beyond the wilderness, struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young people, and they died. I alone escaped to tell you.”

verses.rationale: Keep grief’s bodily acts alongside worship rather than treating them as opposites.
verses.before: Then Job arose, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground, and bowed down.
verses.after: Job rose, tore his robe, and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground and worshiped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job arose, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground, and bowed down.

verses.rationale: Preserve the puzzling return there and the familiar balanced blessing without forced novelty.
verses.before: He said: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
verses.after: He said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said: “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I shall return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retain the narrator’s limited assessment of Job’s response.
verses.before: In all this Job did not sin and did not charge God with wrongdoing.
verses.after: Through all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all this Job did not sin and did not charge God with wrongdoing.

verses.rationale: Repeat the council scene and the accuser’s explicitly stated presentation.
verses.before: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
verses.after: Another day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD. The accuser also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser also came among them to present himself before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated exchange from the first scene.
verses.before: The LORD said to the accuser, “From where have you come?” The accuser answered the LORD and said, “From roaming through the earth and walking about on it.”
verses.after: The LORD asked the accuser, “Where have you come from?” He answered, “From roaming the earth and walking about on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the accuser, “From where have you come?” The accuser answered the LORD and said, “From roaming through the earth and walking about on it.”

verses.rationale: Keep the disturbing divine admission and without cause; do not explain it away.
verses.before: The LORD said to the accuser, “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil. He still holds fast his integrity, although you incited me against him to swallow him up without cause.”
verses.after: The LORD said, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: a man of integrity, upright, fearing God and turning away from evil. He still holds firmly to his integrity, though you incited me against him to destroy him without cause.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the accuser, “Have you set your heart upon my servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man, fearing God and turning away from evil. He still holds fast his integrity, although you incited me against him to swallow him up without cause.”

verses.rationale: Retain the opaque proverb and its following explanation without inventing an origin.
verses.before: The accuser answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life.
verses.after: The accuser answered the LORD, “Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has for his own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: The accuser answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! All that a man has he will give for his life.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily specificity and the repeated challenge.
verses.before: But now stretch out your hand and touch his bone and his flesh. Surely he will curse you to your face.”
verses.after: But stretch out your hand and touch his bone and flesh. He will surely curse you to your face!”
verses.tsw_comparator: But now stretch out your hand and touch his bone and his flesh. Surely he will curse you to your face.”

verses.rationale: State the new permission and remaining limit plainly.
verses.before: The LORD said to the accuser, “Look, he is in your hand. Only preserve his life.”
verses.after: The LORD said to the accuser, “He is in your hands. Only spare his life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the accuser, “Look, he is in your hand. Only preserve his life.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the agent and whole-body extent without a speculative diagnosis.
verses.before: Then the accuser went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
verses.after: The accuser left the LORD’s presence and struck Job with terrible sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the accuser went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

verses.rationale: Keep the concrete tool, bodily action, and setting.
verses.before: He took a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
verses.after: Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.

verses.rationale: Retain the wife’s direct challenge without adding a motive or caricature.
verses.before: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast your integrity? Curse God and die.”
verses.after: His wife said to him, “Are you still holding firmly to your integrity? Curse God and die!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast your integrity? Curse God and die.”

verses.rationale: Keep the rebuke as Job’s speech and the narrator’s explicit with-his-lips qualification.
verses.before: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Will we receive good from God, and will we not receive trouble?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.after: He answered, “You are speaking like one of the foolish women. Should we accept good from God and not accept adversity?” Through all this, Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we receive good from God, and shall we not receive trouble?” In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

verses.rationale: Preserve all names and origins and the friends’ initial stated purpose.
verses.before: Now three friends of Job heard of all this trouble that had come upon him. Each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed together to come to show him sympathy and comfort him.
verses.after: Three of Job’s friends heard about all the adversity that had come upon him. Each set out from his own home: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed to come together to mourn with him and comfort him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now three friends of Job heard of all this trouble that had come upon him. Each came from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed together to come to show him sympathy and comfort him.

verses.rationale: Keep nonrecognition and the shared physical mourning.
verses.before: When they lifted their eyes from far away, they did not recognize him. They lifted their voices and wept. Each tore his robe, and they threw dust toward heaven upon their heads.
verses.after: When they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They wept aloud, tore their robes, and threw dust into the air over their heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they lifted their eyes from far away, they did not recognize him. They lifted their voices and wept. Each tore his robe, and they threw dust toward heaven upon their heads.

verses.rationale: Preserve the full duration and silence’s stated reason.
verses.before: They sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.
verses.after: They sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. No one spoke a word to him, because they saw how great his pain was.
verses.tsw_comparator: They sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

verses.rationale: Distinguish cursing his day from the earlier challenge to curse God.
verses.before: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.
verses.after: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.

verses.rationale: Keep the speech introduction separate from the poem.
verses.before: Job answered and said:
verses.after: Job said:
verses.tsw_comparator: Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Preserve birth and conception and the personified night.
verses.before: “Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, ‘A male has been conceived.’
verses.after: “Let the day I was born perish, and the night that said, ‘A boy is conceived!’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, ‘A male has been conceived.’

verses.rationale: Retain the threefold undoing of the birth day.
verses.before: Let that day be darkness. Let God above not seek it, and let no light shine upon it.
verses.after: Let that day become darkness. Let God above take no notice of it; let no light shine on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let that day be darkness. Let God above not seek it, and let no light shine upon it.

verses.rationale: Keep darkness reclaiming the day and qualify the rare final term in a note.
verses.before: Let darkness and death-shadow reclaim it; let a cloud settle upon it; let whatever darkens the day terrify it.
verses.after: Let darkness and deep shadow reclaim it. Let a cloud settle over it; let the day’s blackness terrify it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let darkness and death-shadow reclaim it; let a cloud settle upon it; let whatever darkens the day terrify it.

verses.rationale: Follow the pointed rejoicing verb while noting the alternative joining sense.
verses.before: That night—let thick darkness seize it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not enter the number of the months.
verses.after: Let thick darkness seize that night. Let it find no joy among the days of the year; let it never enter the count of the months.
verses.tsw_comparator: That night—let thick darkness seize it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not enter the number of the months.

verses.rationale: Preserve barrenness as the night’s wished-for condition.
verses.before: Look, let that night be barren; let no joyful cry enter it.
verses.after: Let that night be barren; let no shout of joy enter it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, let that night be barren; let no joyful cry enter it.

verses.rationale: Keep the ancient chaos creature and curse imagery without rationalizing it.
verses.before: Let people who curse days curse it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.
verses.after: Let those who curse days curse it, those skilled at rousing Leviathan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let those who curse days curse it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.

verses.rationale: Retain the striking dawn image and unfulfilled waiting.
verses.before: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark. Let it wait for light and find none; let it not see the eyelids of dawn,
verses.after: Let its twilight stars go dark. Let it wait for light that never comes, and never see the eyelids of dawn,
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark. Let it wait for light and find none; let it not see the eyelids of dawn,

verses.rationale: Clarify the womb’s referent while preserving its doors.

verses.after: because it did not shut the doors of the womb that bore me and hide trouble from my eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb or hide trouble from my eyes.

verses.rationale: Retain the paired death questions as lament, not instruction.
verses.before: Why did I not die from the womb, come out from the belly and expire?
verses.after: Why did I not die at birth, come out of the womb and breathe my last?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why did I not die from the womb, come out from the belly and expire?

verses.rationale: Keep the bodily images of welcome and nourishment.
verses.before: Why did knees receive me? And why breasts, that I should nurse?
verses.after: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts for me to nurse?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why did knees receive me? And why breasts, that I should nurse?

verses.rationale: Preserve the imagined repose that answers the questions.
verses.before: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept; then I would have been at rest,
verses.after: Then I would be lying down in quiet. I would be asleep and at rest,
verses.tsw_comparator: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept; then I would have been at rest,

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult ruin-building phrase without deciding it means tombs or restored cities.

verses.after: with kings and counselors of the earth who built ruined places for themselves,
verses.tsw_comparator: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built ruins for themselves,

verses.rationale: Retain the parallel wealth images beside death’s leveling.
verses.before: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
verses.after: or with princes who possessed gold and filled their houses with silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

verses.rationale: Preserve the grief-laden birth image without euphemizing it.

verses.after: Or I would be like a buried stillborn child, like infants who never saw the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or why was I not like a hidden miscarriage, like infants who never saw light?

verses.rationale: Keep repeated there and the contrast between agitation and rest.

verses.after: There the wicked stop their raging, and there the exhausted find rest.
verses.tsw_comparator: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary are at rest.

verses.rationale: Preserve the social force of release from coercion.

verses.after: Prisoners are at ease together; they no longer hear the taskmaster’s voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prisoners are at ease together; they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.

verses.rationale: Keep status differences and explicit slavery within the imagined equality.

verses.after: Small and great are there alike, and the slave is free from his master.
verses.tsw_comparator: Small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

verses.rationale: Retain the unanswered question and light/life parallel without adding a named subject.

verses.after: Why is light given to those in misery, and life to those whose souls are bitter,
verses.tsw_comparator: Why is light given to one in misery, and life to the bitter in soul,

verses.after: who rejoice with great joy and are glad when they find a grave?

verses.rationale: Repeat the opening question implicitly and retain the hedge’s changed meaning.

verses.after: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

verses.after: My sighing comes in place of bread, and my groans pour out like water.
verses.tsw_comparator: For my sighing comes before my bread, and my groanings pour out like water.

verses.rationale: Keep the doubled fear and arrival without specifying an earlier anxiety.

verses.after: What I dreaded has overtaken me; what I feared has come upon me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the terror I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has happened to me.

verses.after: I have no ease, no quiet, no rest— only turmoil comes.”

verses.after: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:

verses.after: “If someone ventures a word with you, will you grow weary? Yet who can hold back from speaking?
verses.tsw_comparator: “If someone ventures a word with you, will you become impatient? But who can hold back words?

verses.rationale: Preserve the prior help Eliphaz credits to Job.
verses.before: Look, you have instructed many, and you strengthened weak hands.
verses.after: You have instructed many and strengthened feeble hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, you have instructed many, and you strengthened weak hands.

verses.rationale: Keep the paired bodily images of support.
verses.before: Your words raised up one who was stumbling, and you strengthened knees that were bending.
verses.after: Your words have raised up those who stumbled; you have steadied buckling knees.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your words raised up one who was stumbling, and you strengthened knees that were bending.

verses.rationale: Retain the accusation’s contrast with Job’s former help.
verses.before: But now it comes to you, and you are impatient; it touches you, and you are terrified.
verses.after: But now trouble comes to you, and you grow weary; it touches you, and you are dismayed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now it comes to you, and you are impatient; it touches you, and you are terrified.

verses.rationale: Keep reverence and integrity as the speaker’s proposed grounds of hope.
verses.before: Is not your fear of God your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?
verses.after: Is your reverence not your confidence, your upright way of life your hope?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not your fear of God your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?

verses.rationale: Preserve the friend’s sweeping rhetorical claim as a question.
verses.before: Remember now: who, being innocent, ever perished? And where were the upright ever cut off?
verses.after: Think now: who ever perished while innocent? Where were the upright destroyed?
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember now: who, being innocent, ever perished? And where were the upright ever cut off?

verses.rationale: Keep the agricultural sequence and appeal to observation.
verses.before: As I have seen, people who plow trouble and sow harm reap it.
verses.after: As I have seen, those who plow wrongdoing and sow trouble reap it.
verses.tsw_comparator: As I have seen, those who plow trouble and sow harm reap it.

verses.rationale: Retain breath and anger as parallel destructive images.
verses.before: By the breath of God they perish, and by the wind of his anger they are consumed.
verses.after: At God’s breath they perish; at the blast of his anger they come to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: By the breath of God they perish, and by the wind of his anger they are consumed.

verses.rationale: Supply fall silent to complete the compressed first line, retaining the teeth image.
verses.before: The roar of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.
verses.after: The lion’s roar and the fierce lion’s voice fall silent; the young lions’ teeth are broken.
verses.tsw_comparator: The roar of the lion, the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken.

verses.rationale: Keep the distinct adult and cub outcomes.
verses.before: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
verses.after: The strong lion dies for lack of prey, and the lioness’s cubs are scattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The strong lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

verses.rationale: Preserve secret arrival and partial hearing.
verses.before: Now a word came secretly to me, and my ear received a whisper of it,
verses.after: A word came stealing to me; my ear caught a whisper of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now a word came secretly to me, and my ear received a whisper of it,

verses.rationale: Keep the visionary setting without endorsing the vision’s authority.
verses.before: amid troubling thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls upon people.
verses.after: Amid troubling thoughts from visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
verses.tsw_comparator: amid troubling thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls upon people.

verses.rationale: Retain the bodily intensity of the claimed experience.
verses.before: Dread came upon me, and trembling, and made all my bones shake.
verses.after: fear and trembling came over me, shaking all my bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Dread came upon me, and trembling, and made all my bones shake.

verses.rationale: Preserve spirit or wind ambiguity in a note.
verses.before: A spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.
verses.after: A spirit passed before my face; the hair on my body stood on end.
verses.tsw_comparator: A spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up.

verses.rationale: Keep the unrecognized form and silence preceding speech.
verses.before: It stood still, but I could not recognize its appearance. A form was before my eyes; there was silence, then I heard a voice:
verses.after: It stood still, but I could not make out its appearance. A shape was before my eyes. There was silence, and then I heard a voice:
verses.tsw_comparator: It stood still, but I could not recognize its appearance. A form was before my eyes; there was silence, then I heard a voice:

verses.rationale: Use before while noting the possible comparative more-than reading.
verses.before: ‘Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?
verses.after: ‘Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can a man be pure before his Maker?

verses.rationale: Retain the heavenly servants and unspecified fault.
verses.before: Look, he does not trust his servants, and he charges his messengers with error.
verses.after: He does not trust even his servants; he finds fault with his messengers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he does not trust his servants, and he charges his messengers with error.

verses.rationale: Preserve the fragile dwelling image and qualify the moth comparison in a note.
verses.before: How much more people who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth.
verses.after: How much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in dust, who are crushed more easily than a moth!
verses.tsw_comparator: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before a moth.

verses.rationale: Retain the brief span and absence of notice.
verses.before: Between morning and evening they are broken; without anyone noticing, they perish forever.
verses.after: Between morning and evening they are shattered; unnoticed, they perish forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Between morning and evening they are broken; without anyone noticing, they perish forever.

verses.rationale: Keep the tent image and close the reported voice here.
verses.before: Is not their tent-cord pulled up within them? They die, and not in wisdom.’”
verses.after: Is not their tent cord pulled up? They die without wisdom.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not their tent-cord pulled up within them? They die, and not in wisdom.’”

verses.rationale: Preserve the challenge and heavenly holy ones.
verses.before: “Call out, if you will. Is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
verses.after: Call out now! Is anyone answering you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Call out, if you will. Is there anyone who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

verses.rationale: Keep the paired passions and their claimed results.
verses.before: For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy puts the simple to death.
verses.after: Resentment kills the fool, and jealousy brings death to the simple.
verses.tsw_comparator: For vexation kills the fool, and jealousy puts the simple to death.

verses.rationale: Retain Eliphaz’s own cursing action rather than making it an impersonal event.
verses.before: I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.
verses.after: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.

verses.rationale: Keep the legal-social setting and vulnerable children.
verses.before: His children are far from safety; they are crushed at the gate, and there is no one to deliver them.
verses.after: His children are far from safety; they are crushed at the city gate, with no one to rescue them.
verses.tsw_comparator: His children are far from safety; they are crushed at the gate, and there is no one to deliver them.

verses.rationale: Render the difficult final term as thirsty with alternatives noted.
verses.before: The hungry eat his harvest, even taking it from among thorns, and a snare thirsts for his wealth.
verses.after: The hungry eat his harvest, taking it even from among thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hungry eat his harvest, even taking it from among thorns, and a snare thirsts for his wealth.

verses.rationale: Keep the two negated agricultural origins.
verses.before: For trouble does not come out from the dust, and harm does not sprout from the ground.
verses.after: For wrongdoing does not sprout from the dust, nor does trouble grow from the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: For trouble does not come out from the dust, and harm does not sprout from the ground.

verses.rationale: Use sparks for sons of flame with the ancient image explained briefly.
verses.before: But humanity is born for trouble as sparks fly upward.
verses.after: A human being is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
verses.tsw_comparator: But humanity is born for trouble as sparks fly upward.

verses.rationale: Keep this advice in Eliphaz’s first-person hypothetical voice.
verses.before: But as for me, I would seek God, and to God I would commit my cause,
verses.after: But I would seek God; I would lay my case before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, I would seek God, and to God I would commit my cause,

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired limits of human inquiry.
verses.before: who does great things beyond searching, wonders without number;
verses.after: He does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond counting.
verses.tsw_comparator: who does great things beyond searching, wonders without number;

verses.rationale: Retain the concrete beneficent provision.
verses.before: who gives rain upon the face of the earth and sends water upon the fields;
verses.after: He gives rain to the earth and sends water over the fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: who gives rain upon the face of the earth and sends water upon the fields;

verses.rationale: Keep both status and grief reversals.
verses.before: who sets the lowly on high, and people who mourn are lifted to safety;
verses.after: He lifts the lowly high and raises mourners to safety.
verses.tsw_comparator: who sets the lowly on high, and those who mourn are lifted to safety;

verses.rationale: Preserve planning and failed execution.
verses.before: who frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands cannot achieve success;
verses.after: He frustrates the schemes of the shrewd, so their hands achieve no success.
verses.tsw_comparator: who frustrates the plans of the crafty, so that their hands cannot achieve success;

verses.rationale: Retain the trap in one’s own cunning, not a condemnation of all wisdom.
verses.before: who catches the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the cunning is hurried away.
verses.after: He catches the wise in their own cunning, and the plans of the devious are swept away.
verses.tsw_comparator: who catches the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the cunning is hurried away.

verses.rationale: Keep the paradoxical day and night imagery.
verses.before: By day they meet darkness, and at noon they grope as in the night.
verses.after: They meet darkness in the daytime and grope at noon as though it were night.
verses.tsw_comparator: By day they meet darkness, and at noon they grope as in the night.

verses.rationale: Retain the compressed mouth-sword image and physical power.
verses.before: But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth and from the hand of the strong.
verses.after: But he saves the poor from the sword of their mouths and from the hand of the strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth and from the hand of the strong.

verses.rationale: Keep personified injustice and the resulting hope.
verses.before: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
verses.after: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserve Eliphaz’s interpretation of suffering as correction, not narrator endorsement.
verses.before: Look, blessed is the person whom God corrects; so do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
verses.after: Happy is the person God corrects! Do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, blessed is the person whom God corrects; therefore do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.

verses.rationale: Follow the plural hands reading and balanced actions.
verses.before: For he wounds, but he binds up; he strikes, but his hands heal.
verses.after: For he wounds, but he binds up; he strikes, but his hands heal.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he wounds, but he binds up; he strikes, but his hands heal.

verses.rationale: Retain the ascending numerical saying rather than literalizing a fixed quota.
verses.before: From six troubles he will deliver you, and in seven no harm will touch you.
verses.after: He will rescue you from six troubles; in seven, harm will not touch you.
verses.tsw_comparator: From six troubles he will deliver you, and in seven no harm will touch you.

verses.rationale: Keep redemption and the two dangers.
verses.before: In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
verses.after: In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the power of the sword.

verses.rationale: Retain speech as a lash and the promised protection.
verses.before: From the lash of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear when destruction comes.
verses.after: You will be sheltered from the scourge of the tongue; you will not fear destruction when it comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the lash of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear when destruction comes.

verses.rationale: Preserve the extravagant assurance in the friend’s voice.
verses.before: At destruction and famine you will laugh, and you will not fear the animals of the earth.
verses.after: You will laugh at destruction and famine; you need not fear the earth’s wild animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: At destruction and famine you will laugh, and you will not fear the animals of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep the unusual nonhuman covenant partners.
verses.before: For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the animals of the field will be at peace with you.
verses.after: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the animals of the field will be at peace with you.

verses.rationale: Render the final missing sense without importing a claim of sinlessness.
verses.before: You will know that your tent is at peace; you will inspect your dwelling and miss nothing.
verses.after: You will know that your tent is secure; you will inspect your dwelling and find nothing missing.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will know that your tent is at peace; you will inspect your dwelling and miss nothing.

verses.rationale: Keep the painful promise of children in its context after Job’s loss.
verses.before: You will know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
verses.after: You will know that your descendants are many, your offspring like the grass of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will know that your offspring are many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain the harvest-death comparison and uncertain vigor term.
verses.before: You will come to the grave in full age, like a stack of grain gathered in its season.
verses.after: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf brought in at its proper season.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will come to the grave in full age, like a stack of grain gathered in its season.

verses.rationale: Keep the plural authority claim and direct closing exhortation.
verses.before: Look, this we have searched out; it is so. Hear it, and know it for yourself.”
verses.after: We have examined this, and so it is. Listen to it and know it for yourself.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, this we have searched out; it is so. Hear it, and know it for yourself.”

verses.rationale: Mark the return to Job’s own voice.
verses.before: Then Job answered and said:
verses.after: Then Job answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Preserve the request to assess grief’s true weight.
verses.before: “If only my grief could truly be weighed, and my calamity laid together on the scales!
verses.after: “If only my anguish could be weighed and all my calamity laid together on the scales!
verses.tsw_comparator: “If only my grief could truly be weighed, and my calamity laid together on the scales!

verses.rationale: Keep the overwhelming comparison and Job’s explanation of his speech.
verses.before: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; so my words have been rash.
verses.after: It would outweigh the sand of the seas. That is why my words have been rash.
verses.tsw_comparator: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; therefore my words have been rash.

verses.rationale: Retain Job’s direct attribution and military bodily imagery.
verses.before: For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of God are arranged against me.
verses.after: The Almighty’s arrows are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. God’s terrors are arrayed against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. The terrors of God are arranged against me.

verses.rationale: Keep the animal questions implying a reason for complaint.
verses.before: Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or does the ox low over its fodder?
verses.after: Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does the wild donkey bray over grass, or does the ox low over its fodder?

verses.rationale: Use the traditional egg interpretation with the uncertain plant alternative noted.
verses.before: Can tasteless food be eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?
verses.after: Can tasteless food be eaten without salt? Is there flavor in the white of an egg?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can tasteless food be eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg?

verses.rationale: Preserve disgust without assigning a specific referent to the food.
verses.before: My life refuses to touch them; they are like sickening food to me.
verses.after: I refuse to touch such things; they are like sickening food to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My life refuses to touch them; they are like sickening food to me.

verses.rationale: Keep the petition open until the next verse.
verses.before: If only my request would come, and God would grant my hope—
verses.after: If only my request would be granted, if God would give me what I long for!
verses.tsw_comparator: If only my request would come, and God would grant my hope—

verses.rationale: Preserve the wish for God to end his life without softening it.
verses.before: that God would be willing to crush me, that he would release his hand and cut me off!
verses.after: If only God would consent to crush me, release his hand and cut me off!
verses.tsw_comparator: that God would be willing to crush me, that he would release his hand and cut me off!

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult exultation and Job’s claim of fidelity.
verses.before: Then this would still be my comfort; I would leap in pain that does not spare, for I have not hidden the words of the Holy One.
verses.after: Then I would still have this comfort, and exult in pain that does not relent: I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then this would still be my comfort; I would leap in pain that does not spare, for I have not hidden the words of the Holy One.

verses.rationale: Retain the two questions challenging prolonged hope.
verses.before: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?
verses.after: What strength do I have to keep waiting? What future do I have to prolong my endurance?
verses.tsw_comparator: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?

verses.rationale: Keep the impossible bodily materials rather than paraphrasing invulnerability.
verses.before: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
verses.after: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh bronze?

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired loss of capacity and aid.
verses.before: Is there any help in me? Has resourcefulness been driven from me?
verses.after: Have I not been left without help within me? Has every resource been driven from me?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there any help in me? Has resourcefulness been driven from me?

verses.rationale: Choose the concessive reading while noting a possible accusation against the unkind friend.
verses.before: Steadfast love is owed to one who is despairing by a friend, even if he abandons the fear of the Almighty.
verses.after: A friend owes faithful love to one who is wasting away, even if he abandons reverence for the Almighty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Steadfast love is owed to one who is despairing by a friend, even if he abandons the fear of the Almighty.

verses.rationale: Retain brothers as Job’s relational appeal and begin the extended seasonal-water image.
verses.before: My brothers have dealt treacherously like a wadi, like channels of wadis that pass away,
verses.after: My brothers have been treacherous like a streambed, like channels whose waters pass away,
verses.tsw_comparator: My brothers have dealt treacherously like a wadi, like channels of wadis that pass away,

verses.rationale: Keep the winter abundance preceding disappointment.
verses.before: which are dark with ice, and snow hides itself in them.
verses.after: dark with ice, where snow lies hidden.
verses.tsw_comparator: which are dark with ice, and snow hides itself in them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the seasonal disappearance and emptied location.
verses.before: In the season when they are scorched, they vanish; when it is hot, they disappear from their place.
verses.after: When heat comes, they vanish; in the warmth they dry up where they stood.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the season when they are scorched, they vanish; when it is hot, they disappear from their place.

verses.rationale: Make caravans the travelers while noting the possible watercourse reading.
verses.before: Caravans turn aside from their course; they go up into the wasteland and perish.
verses.after: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Caravans turn aside from their course; they go up into the wasteland and perish.

verses.rationale: Keep both named trading groups and their expectation.
verses.before: The caravans of Tema look; the travelers of Sheba hope for them.
verses.after: The caravans of Tema look for them; the travelers of Sheba hope for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The caravans of Tema look; the travelers of Sheba hope for them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the betrayal of expectation without inventing rescue.
verses.before: They are ashamed because they trusted; they come there and are confounded.
verses.after: They are ashamed because they trusted; they arrive there and are dismayed.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are ashamed because they trusted; they come there and are confounded.

verses.rationale: Use the contextual comparison amid the written/read difficulty, explained in a note.
verses.before: For now you have become nothing; you see terror and are afraid.
verses.after: That is what you have become to me. You see something dreadful and are afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: For now you have become nothing; you see terror and are afraid.

verses.rationale: Keep the denied requests in Job’s defense.
verses.before: Did I say, ‘Give to me’? Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth’?
verses.after: Have I said, ‘Give me something,’ or, ‘Pay a ransom for me from your wealth,’
verses.tsw_comparator: Did I say, ‘Give to me’? Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth’?

verses.rationale: Retain rescue and redemption as distinct parallel appeals.
verses.before: Or, ‘Deliver me from the hand of an adversary’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the ruthless’?
verses.after: or, ‘Rescue me from an enemy’s hand; redeem me from the grip of ruthless men’?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or, ‘Deliver me from the hand of an adversary’? Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the ruthless’?

verses.rationale: Keep willingness to hear evidence rather than conceding guilt.
verses.before: Teach me, and I will be silent; make me understand how I have gone astray.
verses.after: Teach me, and I will be silent. Show me where I have gone wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Teach me, and I will be silent; make me understand how I have gone astray.

verses.rationale: Preserve the contrast between honest speech and unsupported accusation.
verses.before: How forceful are honest words! But what does your correction correct?
verses.after: How forceful honest words can be! But what does your rebuke prove?
verses.tsw_comparator: How forceful are honest words! But what does your correction correct?

verses.rationale: Keep the complaint that despair’s words are being treated as empty air.
verses.before: Do you intend to correct words, and treat the words of one in despair as wind?
verses.after: Do you mean to correct mere words, treating a desperate man’s speech as wind?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you intend to correct words, and treat the words of one in despair as wind?

verses.rationale: Retain the severe social accusation and friend’s betrayal.
verses.before: You would even cast lots over an orphan and bargain over your friend.
verses.after: You would even cast lots over an orphan and bargain away your friend.
verses.tsw_comparator: You would even cast lots over an orphan and bargain over your friend.

verses.rationale: Keep the demand for personal attention and direct challenge.
verses.before: But now, please turn and look at me; surely I will not lie to your face.
verses.after: Now, please turn and look at me. Would I lie to your faces?
verses.tsw_comparator: But now, please turn and look at me; surely I will not lie to your face.

verses.rationale: Follow the repeated imperative and retain righteousness as the disputed issue.
verses.before: Turn, please; let there be no injustice. Turn again; my righteousness is still in this.
verses.after: Reconsider, please; let there be no injustice. Reconsider—my righteousness is at stake.
verses.tsw_comparator: Turn, please; let there be no injustice. Turn again; my righteousness is still in this.

verses.rationale: Preserve the mouth and taste images linking discernment to suffering.
verses.before: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamity?”
verses.after: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamity?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can my palate not discern calamity?”

verses.rationale: Keep the assigned labor image rather than a generic statement that life is hard.
verses.before: “Does not a human have hard service on earth? Are not his days like the days of a hired worker?
verses.after: Does not a mortal have hard service on earth, his days like a hired worker’s?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Does not a human have hard service on earth? Are not his days like the days of a hired worker?

verses.rationale: Retain the distinction between enslaved and hired labor.
verses.before: Like a servant longing for shade, and like a hired worker waiting for wages,
verses.after: Like a slave longing for shade, like a hired worker waiting for his wages,
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a servant longing for shade, and like a hired worker waiting for wages,

verses.rationale: Keep the imposed allotment and differing units of time.
verses.before: so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
verses.after: so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of trouble have been assigned to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.

verses.rationale: Render the difficult night phrase as its experienced length.
verses.before: When I lie down, I say, ‘When will I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am filled with restlessness until dawn.
verses.after: When I lie down, I ask, ‘When can I get up?’ The night drags on, and I am full of tossing until dawn.
