verses.after: though you know that I am not wicked and that no one can rescue me from your hand?
verses.tsw_comparator: though you know that I am not wicked, and there is no one who can deliver from your hand?

verses.rationale: Keep the contradiction between creation and destruction.
verses.before: Your hands shaped me and made me, together all around—yet you swallow me up.
verses.after: Your hands shaped me and made me, every part of me; yet now you destroy me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your hands shaped me and made me, together all around—yet you swallow me up.

verses.rationale: Retain the maker’s materials and reversal.
verses.before: Remember, please, that you made me like clay. Will you return me to dust?
verses.after: Remember, please, that you made me like clay. Will you turn me back to dust?
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember, please, that you made me like clay. Will you return me to dust?

verses.rationale: Preserve the ancient bodily-formation images without modern biological substitution.
verses.before: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,
verses.after: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
verses.tsw_comparator: Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,

verses.rationale: Keep the clothing and joining images in sequence.
verses.before: clothe me with skin and flesh, and weave me together with bones and sinews?
verses.after: You clothed me with skin and flesh and knit me together with bones and sinews.
verses.tsw_comparator: clothe me with skin and flesh, and weave me together with bones and sinews?

verses.rationale: Retain earlier divine care before Job’s suspicion.
verses.before: You gave me life and steadfast love, and your care guarded my spirit.
verses.after: You gave me life and faithful love; your care guarded my spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: You gave me life and steadfast love, and your care guarded my spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserve the accusation of concealed purpose and its continuation.
verses.before: Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was with you:
verses.after: Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know this was your intent:
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was with you:

verses.rationale: Keep conditional sin and unrelenting observation.
verses.before: if I sin, you watch me and do not acquit me of my guilt.
verses.after: if I sinned, you would watch me and would not acquit me of wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: if I sin, you watch me and do not acquit me of my guilt.

verses.rationale: Retain both alternatives and the direct imperative to look.
verses.before: If I am wicked, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am filled with disgrace and look upon my affliction.
verses.after: If I am wicked, woe to me! Even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of disgrace—look at my affliction!
verses.tsw_comparator: If I am wicked, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am filled with disgrace and look upon my affliction.

verses.rationale: Make the raised head implicit from the prior verse and retain wonders used against Job.
verses.before: If my head rises, you hunt me like a lion and again show yourself wondrous against me.
verses.after: If my head rises, you hunt me like a lion and again display your wondrous power against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: If my head rises, you hunt me like a lion and again show yourself wondrous against me.

verses.rationale: Keep courtroom witnesses and repeated military assault.
verses.before: You renew your witnesses against me and increase your anger with me; changes and warfare are against me.
verses.after: You renew your witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; wave after wave of troops comes against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: You renew your witnesses against me and increase your anger with me; changes and warfare are against me.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated birth lament.
verses.before: Why then did you bring me out from the womb? I should have expired, and no eye would have seen me.
verses.after: Why did you bring me out of the womb? If only I had died before any eye saw me!
verses.tsw_comparator: Why then did you bring me out from the womb? I should have expired, and no eye would have seen me.

verses.rationale: Keep the compressed life course and nonexistence wish.
verses.before: I would have been as if I had not been, carried from womb to grave.
verses.after: I would be as though I had never existed, carried straight from the womb to the grave.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would have been as though I had not been, carried from womb to grave.

verses.rationale: Follow the imperative reading tradition and preserve the modest respite sought.
verses.before: Are not my days few? Stop, and leave me alone, that I may brighten a little
verses.after: Are not my days few? Stop, then; leave me alone, so I may find a little cheer,
verses.tsw_comparator: Are not my days few? Stop, and leave me alone, that I may brighten a little

verses.rationale: Keep the irreversible journey as Job’s expectation.
verses.before: before I go—and do not return— to the land of darkness and death-shadow,
verses.after: before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deep shadow,
verses.tsw_comparator: before I go—and do not return— to the land of darkness and death-shadow,

verses.rationale: Retain the layered darkness and final paradox rather than flattening the imagery.
verses.before: a land of deepest gloom, like death-shadow without order, where light is like darkness.”
verses.after: a land of gloom like thick darkness, of deep shadow without order, where even its light is like darkness.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: a land of deepest gloom, like death-shadow without order, where light is like darkness.”

verses.rationale: Identify the third friend and his origin.
verses.before: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
verses.after: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:

verses.rationale: Keep the attack on speech and judicial self-vindication.
verses.before: “Should a multitude of words go unanswered, and should a man full of talk be justified?
verses.after: “Should this torrent of words go unanswered? Does a man win his case by talking?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Should a multitude of words go unanswered, and should a man full of talk be justified?

verses.rationale: Preserve Zophar’s accusation and proposed shaming.
verses.before: Should your empty talk make people silent, and when you mock, should no one shame you?
verses.after: Should your empty talk silence people? Will you mock with no one to shame you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Should your empty talk make people silent, and when you mock, should no one shame you?

verses.rationale: Keep this as Zophar’s representation of Job’s words.
verses.before: For you say, ‘My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes.’
verses.after: You say, ‘My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For you say, ‘My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your eyes.’

verses.rationale: Retain the wish for a divine answer directed against Job.
verses.before: But if only God would speak and open his lips with you,
verses.after: If only God would speak and open his lips against you!
verses.tsw_comparator: But if only God would speak and open his lips with you,

verses.rationale: Keep the difficult doubled wisdom and shocking claim of underpunishment, with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: and tell you the secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom has many sides. Know then that God causes some of your guilt to be forgotten.
verses.after: If only he would tell you wisdom’s secrets, for sound wisdom has a double depth! Know this: God overlooks some of your guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: and tell you the secrets of wisdom, for sound wisdom has many sides. Know then that God causes some of your guilt to be forgotten.

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired limits of inquiry.
verses.before: Can you search out the depths of God? Can you find the limit of the Almighty?
verses.after: Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you reach the limits of the Almighty?
verses.tsw_comparator: Can you search out the depths of God? Can you find the limit of the Almighty?

verses.rationale: Keep the cosmic extremes and separate action from knowledge.
verses.before: It is higher than heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
verses.after: They are higher than heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
verses.tsw_comparator: It is higher than heaven—what can you do? Deeper than Sheol—what can you know?

verses.rationale: Retain the horizontal dimensions after the vertical ones.
verses.before: Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
verses.after: Their measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.

verses.rationale: Keep the judicial sequence and unchallengeable power.
verses.before: If he passes through and imprisons and summons an assembly, who can turn him back?
verses.after: If he passes by, imprisons someone, and calls the court, who can stop him?
verses.tsw_comparator: If he passes through and imprisons and summons an assembly, who can turn him back?

verses.rationale: Choose effortless discernment while noting the possible rhetorical question.
verses.before: For he knows people of emptiness; when he sees wickedness, will he not consider it?
verses.after: He knows deceitful people; he sees wrongdoing without needing to investigate.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he knows people of emptiness; when he sees wickedness, will he not consider it?

verses.rationale: Retain the biting impossibility comparison, with the alternative developmental reading noted.
verses.before: But an empty-headed person may gain understanding when a wild donkey’s colt is born human.
verses.after: An empty-headed man will gain understanding when a wild donkey’s colt is born human!
verses.tsw_comparator: But an empty-headed person may gain understanding when a wild donkey’s colt is born human.

verses.rationale: Preserve inner preparation and bodily petition.
verses.before: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward him,
verses.after: If you set your heart right and spread your hands toward him,
verses.tsw_comparator: If you prepare your heart and stretch out your hands toward him,

verses.rationale: Retain hand and dwelling as sites of wrongdoing.
verses.before: if wickedness is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice dwell in your tents,
verses.after: if you put the wrongdoing in your hands far away and let no injustice live in your tents,
verses.tsw_comparator: if wickedness is in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice dwell in your tents,

verses.rationale: Keep the promised reversal contingent on the preceding demands.
verses.before: then surely you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be firm and will not fear.
verses.after: then you will lift your face without blemish; you will stand firm and have no fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: then surely you will lift up your face without blemish; you will be firm and will not fear.

verses.rationale: Preserve the vanishing-water comparison.
verses.before: For you will forget your misery, remembering it only as waters that have passed by.
verses.after: You will forget your trouble, remembering it as water that has flowed away.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will forget your misery, remembering it only as waters that have passed by.

verses.rationale: Keep the doubled light reversal and uncertain darkness term.
verses.before: Your lifetime will rise brighter than noon; darkness will become like morning.
verses.after: Your life will rise brighter than noon; even its darkness will be like morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your lifetime will rise brighter than noon; darkness will become like morning.

verses.rationale: Use look around for the difficult verb, with digging as an alternative.
verses.before: You will trust because there is hope; you will look around and lie down securely.
verses.after: You will feel secure because there is hope; you will look around and lie down safely.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will trust because there is hope; you will look around and lie down securely.

verses.rationale: Retain physical safety and restored social standing.
verses.before: You will lie down with no one making you afraid, and many will seek your favor.
verses.after: You will rest with no one to frighten you, and many will seek your favor.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will lie down with no one making you afraid, and many will seek your favor.

verses.rationale: Keep the closing threat and hope reduced to dying.
verses.before: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; escape will perish from them, and their hope will be the breathing out of life.”
verses.after: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; escape will elude them, and their only hope will be their last breath.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the eyes of the wicked will fail; escape will perish from them, and their hope will be the breathing out of life.”

verses.rationale: Mark Job’s extended reply.
verses.before: Then Job answered and said:
verses.after: Then Job answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Preserve the sarcasm without adding explanatory narration.
verses.before: “Truly you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
verses.after: “Surely you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
verses.tsw_comparator: “Truly you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!

verses.rationale: Keep the claim to equal understanding and commonplace knowledge.
verses.before: Yet I also have a heart like you; I am not inferior to you. And who does not know things like these?
verses.after: But I have understanding as you do; I am no less than you. Who does not know such things?
verses.tsw_comparator: But I also have a heart like you; I am not inferior to you. And who does not know things like these?

verses.rationale: Preserve the personal contrast and repeated ridicule.
verses.before: I have become a laughingstock to my neighbor, one who called to God and he answered him— a laughingstock: the righteous and blameless man.
verses.after: I have become a laughingstock to my friend— I who called on God and received an answer, a righteous man of integrity, made a joke.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have become a laughingstock to my neighbor, one who called to God and he answered him— a laughingstock: the righteous and blameless man.

verses.rationale: Keep the criticism of secure observers and the difficult disaster clause.
verses.before: In the thought of one who is at ease, there is contempt for disaster, ready for those whose foot slips.
verses.after: Those at ease think disaster deserves contempt; it awaits those whose feet slip.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thought of one who is at ease, there is contempt for disaster, ready for those whose foot slips.

verses.rationale: Choose the hand-carried god reading while noting God’s provision as an alternative.
verses.before: The tents of robbers are at peace, and people who provoke God are secure, people who bring their god in their hand.
verses.after: Robbers’ tents are peaceful, and those who provoke God are secure— those who carry their god in their hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God are secure, those who bring their god in their hand.

verses.rationale: Keep nonhuman creatures as teachers.
verses.before: But ask the animals, and they will teach you; the birds of the heavens, and they will tell you.
verses.after: Ask the animals, and they will teach you; the birds of the heavens will tell you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But ask the animals, and they will teach you; the birds of the heavens, and they will tell you.

verses.rationale: Retain earth and fish as voices in the argument.
verses.before: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; and the fish of the sea will recount it to you.
verses.after: Speak to the earth, and it will teach you; the fish of the sea will recount it to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; and the fish of the sea will recount it to you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the divine name’s unusual appearance in the dialogue.
verses.before: Who among all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
verses.after: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who among all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?

verses.rationale: Keep the universal living scope and breath distinction.
verses.before: In whose hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all human flesh.
verses.after: In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all humanity.
verses.tsw_comparator: In whose hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all human flesh.

verses.rationale: Retain sensory discernment as a model for judging speech.
verses.before: Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
verses.after: Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?

verses.rationale: Keep the traditional saying before its divine comparison.
verses.before: Is wisdom with the aged, and understanding in length of days?
verses.after: Wisdom is with the aged, and understanding with length of days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Is wisdom with the aged, and understanding in length of days?

verses.rationale: Clarify the pronoun’s divine referent and retain all four terms.
verses.before: With him are wisdom and strength; his are counsel and understanding.
verses.after: With God are wisdom and might; counsel and understanding belong to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: With him are wisdom and strength; his are counsel and understanding.

verses.rationale: Keep the parallel irreversibility of destruction and confinement.
verses.before: Look, he tears down, and it cannot be rebuilt; he shuts a man in, and no one can open.
verses.after: What he tears down cannot be rebuilt; whoever he shuts in cannot be released.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he tears down, and it cannot be rebuilt; he shuts a man in, and no one can open.

verses.rationale: Retain both drought and flood under divine agency.
verses.before: Look, he withholds the waters, and they dry up; he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.
verses.after: If he holds back the waters, they dry up; if he sends them out, they overturn the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, he withholds the waters, and they dry up; he sends them out, and they overturn the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve the morally unsettling paired ownership.
verses.before: With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are his.
verses.after: With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver belong to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are his.

verses.rationale: Keep the humiliation of political wisdom.
verses.before: He leads counselors away stripped and makes judges fools.
verses.after: He leads counselors away stripped and makes fools of judges.
verses.tsw_comparator: He leads counselors away stripped and makes judges fools.

verses.rationale: Preserve the bond reversal while noting royal insignia as another reading.
verses.before: He loosens the discipline of kings and binds a belt around their waist.
verses.after: He loosens the bonds imposed by kings and binds a belt around their waists.
verses.tsw_comparator: He loosens the discipline of kings and binds a belt around their waist.

verses.rationale: Keep priestly humiliation and collapse of entrenched power.
verses.before: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the established.
verses.after: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the firmly established.
verses.tsw_comparator: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the established.

verses.rationale: Retain loss of voice and judgment.
verses.before: He removes speech from the trusted and takes away discernment from elders.
verses.after: He removes the speech of trusted advisors and takes away the elders’ discernment.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removes speech from the trusted and takes away discernment from elders.

verses.rationale: Keep poured contempt and weakened strength in bodily imagery.
verses.before: He pours contempt upon nobles and loosens the belt of the strong.
verses.after: He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: He pours contempt upon nobles and loosens the belt of the strong.

verses.rationale: Preserve the paired unveiling images.
verses.before: He uncovers deep things from darkness and brings death-shadow into light.
verses.after: He uncovers deep things from darkness and brings deep shadow into the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: He uncovers deep things from darkness and brings death-shadow into light.

verses.rationale: Keep both expansion and undoing without assigning a modern political lesson.
verses.before: He makes nations great and destroys them; he enlarges nations and leads them away.
verses.after: He makes nations great and destroys them; he spreads nations abroad and leads them away.
verses.tsw_comparator: He makes nations great and destroys them; he enlarges nations and leads them away.

verses.rationale: Retain the loss of heart as understanding and resulting disorientation.
verses.before: He removes the heart from the heads of the people of the earth and makes them wander in a wasteland without a way.
verses.after: He takes understanding from the leaders of the earth’s people and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
verses.tsw_comparator: He removes the heart from the heads of the people of the earth and makes them wander in a wasteland without a way.

verses.rationale: Keep the final blindness and intoxication comparison.
verses.before: They grope in darkness with no light, and he makes them wander like a drunken person.”
verses.after: They grope in darkness without light; he makes them stagger like a drunkard.
verses.tsw_comparator: They grope in darkness with no light, and he makes them wander like a drunken person.”

verses.rationale: Retain Job’s appeal to his own perception.
verses.before: “Look, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.
verses.after: My eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood it.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.

verses.rationale: Repeat the equal-standing claim from 12:3.
verses.before: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
verses.after: What you know, I know too. I am no less than you.
verses.tsw_comparator: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.

verses.rationale: Keep Job’s chosen interlocutor and legal desire.
verses.before: Yet I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.
verses.after: But I want to speak to the Almighty; I desire to argue my case with God.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to argue my case with God.

verses.rationale: Preserve the plastering and failed-healing images.
verses.before: But you smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
verses.after: You smear things over with lies; all of you are worthless physicians.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.

verses.rationale: Keep the pointed reversal of their wisdom claims.
verses.before: If only you would be completely silent! That would become your wisdom.
verses.after: If only you would be completely silent! That would be wisdom for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If only you would be completely silent! That would become your wisdom.

verses.rationale: Retain the demand for a hearing and speaking lips.
verses.before: Hear now my argument, and listen to the contentions of my lips.
verses.after: Listen, please, to my argument; attend to the case my lips present.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear now my argument, and listen to the contentions of my lips.

verses.rationale: Preserve the challenge to dishonest religious defense.
verses.before: Will you speak injustice for God? Will you speak deceitfully for him?
verses.after: Will you speak injustice on God’s behalf and tell lies for him?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you speak injustice for God? Will you speak deceitfully for him?

verses.rationale: Keep the courtroom charge of favoritism even toward God.
verses.before: Will you show partiality toward him? Will you contend for God?
verses.after: Will you show partiality toward him? Will you plead God’s case?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you show partiality toward him? Will you contend for God?

verses.rationale: Retain the reversal of who faces divine scrutiny.
verses.before: Would it be good if he examined you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a human?
verses.after: Will it go well when he examines you? Can you deceive him as you deceive a mortal?
verses.tsw_comparator: Would it be good if he examined you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a human?

verses.rationale: Preserve emphatic correction and concealed bias.
verses.before: He would surely correct you if in secret you show partiality.
verses.after: He will surely rebuke you if you secretly show partiality.
verses.tsw_comparator: He would surely correct you if in secret you show partiality.

verses.rationale: Keep the two fear images directed at the friends.
verses.before: Would not his majesty terrify you, and dread of him fall upon you?
verses.after: Will not his majesty terrify you, and dread of him fall upon you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Would not his majesty terrify you, and dread of him fall upon you?

verses.rationale: Retain the fragile material metaphors without generic dismissal.
verses.before: Your remembered sayings are proverbs of ash; your defenses are defenses of clay.
verses.after: Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your remembered sayings are proverbs of ash; your defenses are defenses of clay.

verses.rationale: Preserve Job’s acceptance of risk in speaking.
verses.before: Be silent before me, and let me speak; then let come upon me what may.
verses.after: Be silent and let me speak; then let whatever comes come upon me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be silent before me, and let me speak; then let come upon me what may.

verses.rationale: Keep the opaque bodily idioms and interrogative form.
verses.before: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hand?
verses.after: Why should I carry my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hands?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hand?

verses.rationale: Follow the reading tradition’s for him; note the written I have no hope as consequential alternative.
verses.before: Though he kill me, I will hope in him; yet I will argue my ways before his face.
verses.after: He may kill me; still I will wait for him. Yet I will argue my ways to his face.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though he kill me, I will hope in him; yet I will argue my ways before his face.

verses.rationale: Retain Job’s argument from willingness to appear before God.
verses.before: This also will be my salvation, for no godless person can come before him.
verses.after: This too will be my deliverance, for no godless person would come before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: This also will be my salvation, for no godless person can come before him.

verses.rationale: Keep emphatic listening and explanatory purpose.
verses.before: Listen carefully to my words, and let my declaration be in your ears.
verses.after: Listen closely to my words; let my explanation reach your ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen carefully to my words, and let my declaration be in your ears.

verses.rationale: Preserve deliberate preparation and confidence in a right judgment.
verses.before: Look now, I have arranged my case; I know that I am in the right.
verses.after: I have now arranged my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look now, I have arranged my case; I know that I am in the right.

verses.rationale: Keep the challenge and its stark consequence without supplying a challenger.
verses.before: Who is there who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and expire.
verses.after: Who is there to dispute with me? Then I would be silent and breathe my last.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is there who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and expire.

verses.rationale: Mark the turn to God and preserve the numbered request.
verses.before: Only two things do not do to me; then I will not hide from your face:
verses.after: Only grant me these two things; then I will not hide from your face:
verses.tsw_comparator: Only two things do not do to me; then I will not hide from your face:

verses.rationale: Keep the two requested removals.
verses.before: withdraw your hand far from me, and do not let your terror frighten me.
verses.after: withdraw your hand from me, and do not let your terror frighten me.
verses.tsw_comparator: withdraw your hand far from me, and do not let your terror frighten me.

verses.rationale: Preserve the reciprocal hearing Job seeks.
verses.before: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
verses.after: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you answer me.

verses.rationale: Keep the demand for specific charges and repeated sin terms.
verses.before: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.
verses.after: How many are my wrongs and sins? Make my rebellion and my sin known to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my transgression and my sin.

verses.rationale: Retain relational concealment and hostile classification.
verses.before: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?
verses.after: Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you hide your face and consider me your enemy?

verses.rationale: Keep the disproportionate pursuit of fragile objects.
verses.before: Will you terrify a driven leaf and pursue dry chaff?
verses.after: Will you terrify a windblown leaf and pursue dry straw?
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you terrify a driven leaf and pursue dry chaff?

verses.rationale: Preserve written accusation and inherited liability.
verses.before: For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
verses.after: You write bitter charges against me and make me inherit the wrongs of my youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you write bitter things against me and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.

verses.rationale: Retain restraint, surveillance, and the difficult footprint-marking image.
verses.before: You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark the soles of my feet.
verses.after: You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark the soles of my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark the soles of my feet.

verses.rationale: Make the generalizing third-person shift readable without attributing it to God.
verses.before: And he wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.”
verses.after: A person wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.”

verses.rationale: Preserve birth, brevity, and trouble rather than flattening human frailty.
verses.before: A human being, born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
verses.after: A human being, born of woman, has few days and is full of turmoil.
verses.tsw_comparator: A human being, born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.

verses.rationale: Keep the paired fleeting images.
verses.before: Like a flower the human comes forth and withers; they flee like a shadow and do not endure.
verses.after: He comes out like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not last.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like a flower the human comes forth and withers; they flee like a shadow and do not endure.

verses.rationale: Retain the move from general humanity to Job himself.
verses.before: And do you fix your gaze on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?
verses.after: Do you fix your eyes even on such a one and bring me into judgment with you?
verses.tsw_comparator: And do you fix your gaze on such a one, and bring me into judgment with you?

verses.rationale: Keep the terse question and answer without adding a doctrine of inherited sin.
verses.before: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one.
verses.after: Who can bring something clean from what is unclean? No one.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? No one.

verses.rationale: Follow the plural limits reading and preserve days/months.
verses.before: Since their days are determined, and the number of their months is with you, and you have appointed their limit that they cannot pass,
verses.after: His days are determined; the number of his months is with you. You have set limits he cannot cross.
verses.tsw_comparator: Since their days are determined, and the number of their months is with you, and you have appointed their limit that they cannot pass,

verses.rationale: Retain the laborer comparison and requested respite.
verses.before: look away from them and let them alone, that they may enjoy, like a hired worker, their day.
verses.after: Look away from him and let him rest, until he enjoys his day like a hired worker.
verses.tsw_comparator: look away from them and let them alone, that they may enjoy, like a hired worker, their day.

verses.rationale: Keep the contrastive tree’s capacity for renewal.
verses.before: For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoots will not cease.
verses.after: There is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it can sprout again, and its shoots need not cease.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoots will not cease.

verses.rationale: Preserve the apparently dead plant parts.
verses.before: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the ground,
verses.after: Though its roots grow old in the earth and its stump dies in the dust,
verses.tsw_comparator: Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the ground,

verses.rationale: Retain the vivid scent-of-water image.
verses.before: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put forth branches like a young plant.
verses.after: at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a young plant.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet at the scent of water it will bud and put forth branches like a young plant.

verses.rationale: Keep the human contrast and unresolved question.
verses.before: But a human dies and is laid low; a person breathes their last—and where are they?
verses.after: But a man dies and lies powerless; a human breathes his last, and where is he?
verses.tsw_comparator: But a human dies and is laid low; a person breathes their last—and where are they?

verses.rationale: Render sea as inland water here without changing the drying image.
verses.before: As waters fail from a lake, and a river wastes away and dries up,
verses.after: Water drains away from a lake; a river runs dry and withers.
verses.tsw_comparator: As waters fail from a lake, and a river wastes away and dries up,

verses.rationale: Preserve the vast temporal limit without turning it into an explicit resurrection prediction.
verses.before: so a human lies down and does not rise; until the heavens are no more they will not awake or be roused out of their sleep.
verses.after: So a person lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, they will not awake or be roused from their sleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: so a human lies down and does not rise; until the heavens are no more they will not awake or be roused out of their sleep.

verses.rationale: Keep the wished-for shelter in death and appointed remembrance.
verses.before: Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would conceal me until your wrath has passed, that you would appoint me a set time and remember me!
verses.after: If only you would hide me in Sheol, conceal me until your anger passes, set a time for me and remember me!
verses.tsw_comparator: Oh that you would hide me in Sheol, that you would conceal me until your wrath has passed, that you would appoint me a set time and remember me!

verses.rationale: Retain the open question and conditional imagined waiting.
verses.before: If a human dies, will they live again? All the days of my service I would wait, until my release should come.
verses.after: If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait until my relief came.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a human dies, will they live again? All the days of my service I would wait, until my release should come.

verses.rationale: Keep the imagined reciprocal relationship and divine longing.
verses.before: You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
verses.after: You would call, and I would answer; you would long for the work of your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.

verses.rationale: Continue the hopeful hypothetical reading, with present scrutiny as an alternative noted.
verses.before: For then you would count my steps; you would not keep watch over my sin.
verses.after: Then you would count my steps but would not keep watch over my sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: For then you would count my steps; you would not keep watch over my sin.

verses.rationale: Preserve the sealed-bag image without asserting whether it stores or removes guilt as certain.
verses.before: My rebellion would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my iniquity.
verses.after: My rebellion would be sealed in a bag; you would cover over my wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: My rebellion would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keep the adversative return from hope to erosion.
verses.before: But the mountain falls and crumbles away, and the rock is moved from its place;
verses.after: But a mountain falls and crumbles, and a rock moves from its place.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the mountain falls and crumbles away, and the rock is moved from its place;

verses.rationale: Retain slow natural destruction as the direct accusation’s comparison.
verses.before: water wears away stones; torrents wash away the dust of the earth— so you destroy the hope of mortals.
verses.after: Water wears away stones; its torrents wash away the soil of the earth. So you destroy a mortal’s hope.
verses.tsw_comparator: water wears away stones; torrents wash away the dust of the earth— so you destroy the hope of mortals.

verses.rationale: Preserve final defeat and altered appearance.
verses.before: You prevail forever against them, and they pass away; you change their countenance, and send them away.
verses.after: You overpower him forever, and he goes away; you change his face and send him off.
verses.tsw_comparator: You prevail forever against them, and they pass away; you change their countenance, and send them away.

verses.rationale: Keep the dead person’s separation from both outcomes for his children.
verses.before: Their children come to honor, and they do not know it; they are brought low, and they do not perceive it.
verses.after: His children gain honor, but he does not know it; they are brought low, but he does not perceive it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their children come to honor, and they do not know it; they are brought low, and they do not perceive it.

verses.rationale: Preserve the difficult closing bodily pain and inward grief without explaining the state of the dead.
verses.before: They feel only the pain of their own body, and their own being mourns.
verses.after: He feels only the pain of his own flesh, and his soul mourns for himself.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They feel only the pain of their own body, and their own being mourns.

verses.rationale: Mark the return of the first friend.
verses.before: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.after: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:

verses.rationale: Preserve the bodily wind insult and specific east wind.
verses.before: “Should a wise man answer with knowledge of wind and fill his belly with the east wind?
verses.after: “Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill his belly with the east wind?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Should a wise man answer with knowledge of wind and fill his belly with the east wind?

verses.rationale: Keep the paired charges of unprofitable speech.
verses.before: Should he argue with a word that does not profit or with speeches by which he does no good?
verses.after: Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good?
verses.tsw_comparator: Should he argue with a word that does not profit or with speeches by which he does no good?

verses.rationale: Preserve Eliphaz’s religious accusation without narrator endorsement.
verses.before: Indeed, you break down the fear of God and diminish meditation before God.
verses.after: You are undermining reverence and diminishing meditation before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed, you break down the fear of God and diminish meditation before God.

verses.rationale: Retain the claimed source of Job’s speech.
verses.before: For your guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
verses.after: Your wrongdoing teaches your mouth what to say; you choose the tongue of the shrewd.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.

verses.rationale: Keep the courtroom mouth-and-lips parallel.
verses.before: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you.
verses.after: Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your lips testify against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I; your own lips testify against you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the primordial questions without explaining an unstated myth.
verses.before: Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
verses.after: Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
verses.tsw_comparator: Were you the first human born? Were you brought forth before the hills?

verses.rationale: Retain the divine council and accusation of monopolized wisdom.
verses.before: Have you listened in the council of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?
verses.after: Have you listened in on God’s council? Have you kept wisdom for yourself?
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you listened in the council of God? Do you limit wisdom to yourself?

verses.rationale: Keep the doubled challenge to superior knowledge.
verses.before: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?
verses.after: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not?
verses.tsw_comparator: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us?

verses.rationale: Preserve the appeal to seniority, not proof of correctness.
verses.before: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older in days than your father.
verses.after: Among us are the gray-haired and the aged, older in days than your father.
verses.tsw_comparator: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older in days than your father.

verses.rationale: Retain Eliphaz’s description of the offered comfort.
verses.before: Are the consolations of God too small for you, or a word spoken gently with you?
verses.after: Are God’s consolations too little for you, and words spoken gently to you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are the consolations of God too small for you, or a word spoken gently with you?

verses.rationale: Keep the inner impulse and outward expression, with the rare eye verb qualified.
verses.before: Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
verses.after: Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
verses.tsw_comparator: Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,

verses.rationale: Preserve the continuation and accusation of opposition to God.
verses.before: that you turn your spirit against God and bring such words out of your mouth?
verses.after: that you turn your spirit against God and let such words out of your mouth?
verses.tsw_comparator: that you turn your spirit against God and bring such words out of your mouth?

verses.rationale: Keep the birth-and-purity question as the friend’s argument.
verses.before: What is a human that he should be pure, or one born of woman that he should be righteous?
verses.after: What is a mortal, that he could be pure, one born of woman, that he could be righteous?
verses.tsw_comparator: What is a human that he should be pure, or one born of woman that he should be righteous?

verses.rationale: Follow the plural holy ones reading and retain the sweeping celestial claim.
verses.before: Look, God does not trust his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his eyes.
verses.after: God does not trust even his holy ones; the heavens are not pure in his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God does not trust his holy ones, and the heavens are not pure in his eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserve the demeaning language and drinking image.
verses.before: How much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a human who drinks injustice like water!
verses.after: How much less one who is detestable and corrupt, a man who drinks injustice like water!
verses.tsw_comparator: How much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a human who drinks injustice like water!

verses.rationale: Keep the personal claim to observation.
verses.before: I will tell you; listen to me. What I have seen I will recount,
verses.after: I will tell you; listen to me. I will recount what I have seen,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will tell you; listen to me. What I have seen I will recount,

verses.rationale: Retain transmitted teaching as a second claimed authority.
verses.before: what wise people have declared and did not hide from their ancestors,
verses.after: what the wise have handed down without hiding what came from their ancestors,
verses.tsw_comparator: what wise people have declared and did not hide from their ancestors,

verses.rationale: Preserve the exclusionary ancestral claim without endorsing its premise.
verses.before: to whom alone the land was given and no stranger passed among them.
verses.after: to whom alone the land was given, with no foreigner passing among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: to whom alone the land was given and no stranger passed among them.

verses.rationale: Keep lifelong torment and the allotted years.
verses.before: The wicked writhes in pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden from the ruthless.
verses.after: The wicked man writhes all his days, through all the years stored up for the ruthless.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wicked writhes in pain all his days, and the number of years is hidden from the ruthless.

verses.rationale: Retain auditory fear and interrupted security.
verses.before: Sounds of terror are in his ears; in peace a destroyer comes upon him.
verses.after: Terrifying sounds fill his ears; in a time of peace a destroyer comes upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sounds of terror are in his ears; in peace a destroyer comes upon him.

verses.rationale: Follow the passive reading tradition and preserve fatal expectation.
verses.before: He does not trust that he will return from darkness; he is destined for the sword.
verses.after: He does not believe he will return from darkness; he is marked out for the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: He does not trust that he will return from darkness; he is destined for the sword.

verses.rationale: Keep the inserted food question and imminent darkness.
verses.before: He wanders for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.after: He wanders in search of bread: ‘Where is it?’ He knows a day of darkness is close at hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: He wanders for bread, saying, ‘Where is it?’ He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.

verses.rationale: Preserve personified distress and the military comparison.
verses.before: Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle,
verses.after: Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle,
verses.tsw_comparator: Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for battle,

verses.rationale: Keep the stated causal accusation and hand gesture.
verses.before: because he stretched out his hand against God and acted defiantly against the Almighty,
verses.after: because he stretched out his hand against God and defied the Almighty,
verses.tsw_comparator: because he stretched out his hand against God and acted defiantly against the Almighty,

verses.rationale: Retain physical battle equipment and stubborn posture.
verses.before: running against him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields.
verses.after: charging against him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields.
verses.tsw_comparator: running against him with a stiff neck, with the thick bosses of his shields.

verses.rationale: Preserve the ancient prosperity image rather than moralizing body size.
verses.before: For he covered his face with fat and put fat upon his waist.
verses.after: Though he has covered his face with fat and gathered fat around his waist,
verses.tsw_comparator: For he covered his face with fat and put fat upon his waist.

verses.rationale: Retain ruined dwellings and their future collapse.
verses.before: He lived in destroyed cities, in houses where no one should dwell, which were ready to become ruins.
verses.after: he lives in destroyed cities, in houses no one should inhabit, places destined to become rubble.
verses.tsw_comparator: He lived in destroyed cities, in houses where no one should dwell, which were ready to become ruins.

verses.rationale: Use possessions for the rare final noun with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: He will not become rich, and his wealth will not endure, and his possessions will not spread over the land.
verses.after: He will not remain rich; his wealth will not endure, and his possessions will not spread over the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will not become rich, and his wealth will not endure, and his possessions will not spread over the land.

verses.rationale: Keep the plant and breath images while clarifying the divine referent.
verses.before: He will not depart from darkness; flame will dry up his shoots, and by the breath of God’s mouth he will depart.
verses.after: He will not escape the darkness. A flame will dry up his shoots, and at the breath of God’s mouth he will depart.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will not depart from darkness; flame will dry up his shoots, and by the breath of God’s mouth he will depart.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated emptiness and recompense.
verses.before: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.
verses.after: Let him not deceive himself by trusting emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.

verses.rationale: Keep premature repayment and loss of vitality.
verses.before: It will be completed before his time, and his branch will not be green.
verses.after: It will be paid in full before his time, and his palm branch will not be green.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will be completed before his time, and his branch will not be green.

verses.rationale: Retain both plants and their failed fruitfulness.
verses.before: He will shake off his unripe grape like a vine and cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
verses.after: He will shed his unripe grapes like a vine and cast off his blossom like an olive tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will shake off his unripe grape like a vine and cast off his blossom like an olive tree.

verses.rationale: Keep collective barrenness and corrupt dwellings.
verses.before: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
verses.after: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.

verses.rationale: Preserve the birth metaphor and repeated production of harm.
verses.before: They conceive trouble and give birth to harm, and their womb prepares deceit.”
verses.after: They conceive trouble and give birth to wrongdoing; their womb prepares deceit.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They conceive trouble and give birth to harm, and their womb prepares deceit.”

verses.rationale: Return clearly to Job.
verses.before: Then Job answered and said:
verses.after: Then Job answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Retain the paradoxical accusation against comforters.
verses.before: “I have heard many things like these. Miserable comforters are you all.
verses.after: “I have heard many things like these. All of you are comforters who bring trouble!
verses.tsw_comparator: “I have heard many things like these. Miserable comforters are you all.

verses.rationale: Keep Job’s reversal of the wind insult and direct challenge.
verses.before: Is there an end to words of wind? Or what provokes you that you answer?
verses.after: Will windy words never end? What drives you to keep answering?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there an end to words of wind? Or what provokes you that you answer?

verses.rationale: Preserve the imagined exchanged positions and mocking gesture.
verses.before: I also could speak as you do if your life were in place of my life. I could compose words against you and shake my head at you.
verses.after: I too could speak as you do, if you were in my place. I could string words together against you and shake my head at you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also could speak as you do if your life were in place of my life. I could compose words against you and shake my head at you.

verses.rationale: Retain the possible sincere or ironic offer without inserting but.
verses.before: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the movement of my lips would bring relief.
verses.after: I could strengthen you with my mouth; the movement of my lips could bring relief.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the movement of my lips would bring relief.

verses.rationale: Keep the failure of both speech and silence.
verses.before: If I speak, my pain is not restrained; and if I stop, what departs from me?
verses.after: If I speak, my pain is not relieved; if I stop, what leaves me?
verses.tsw_comparator: If I speak, my pain is not restrained; and if I stop, what departs from me?

verses.rationale: Preserve the abrupt third-to-second-person shift and total social loss.
verses.before: But now he has worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.
verses.after: But now he has worn me out; you have devastated my whole company.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now he has worn me out. You have made all my company desolate.

verses.rationale: Keep the body as hostile evidence in the legal argument.
verses.before: You have shriveled me, and it has become a witness. My leanness rises against me and testifies to my face.
verses.after: You have shriveled me up, and it has become a witness. My wasting body rises against me and testifies to my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have shriveled me, and it has become a witness. My leanness rises against me and testifies to my face.

verses.rationale: Retain the hostile divine imagery without removing its violence. Focused rereading clarifies the acting subject in English without weakening the accusation.
verses.before: He tears me in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me. My adversary sharpens his eyes against me.
verses.after: He tears me apart in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me. My adversary sharpens his gaze against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He tears me in his anger and hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me. My adversary sharpens his eyes against me.

verses.rationale: Keep the switch to plural attackers and humiliating blows.
verses.before: They open their mouths against me; they strike my cheek with contempt; they gather together against me.
verses.after: They gape at me with their mouths; they strike my cheek in contempt. Together they mass against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: They open their mouths against me; they strike my cheek with contempt; they gather together against me.

verses.rationale: Preserve explicit divine agency in Job’s accusation.
verses.before: God gives me over to unjust men and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
verses.after: God hands me over to the unjust and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
verses.tsw_comparator: God gives me over to unjust men and throws me into the hands of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Keep the three escalating actions and target image.
verses.before: I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and crushed me. He set me up as his target.
verses.after: I was at ease, but he shattered me. He seized me by the neck and crushed me; he set me up as his target.
verses.tsw_comparator: I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and crushed me. He set me up as his target.

verses.rationale: Retain graphic bodily harm and note arrows as an alternative to archers.
verses.before: His archers surround me. He splits open my kidneys and does not spare; he pours my gall upon the ground.
verses.after: His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without pity and pours my gall onto the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: His archers surround me. He splits open my kidneys and does not spare; he pours my gall upon the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserve siege and assault imagery.
verses.before: He breaks me breach upon breach; he runs upon me like a warrior.
verses.after: He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior.
verses.tsw_comparator: He breaks me breach upon breach; he runs upon me like a warrior.

verses.rationale: Keep the strange horn image, explaining diminished strength in vocabulary.
verses.before: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and thrust my horn into the dust.
verses.after: I have sewn sackcloth onto my skin and thrust my horn into the dust.
