verses.before: You will decide a matter, and it will stand for you, and light will shine upon your ways.
verses.after: You will decide on a matter, and it will stand for you; light will shine on your paths.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will decide a matter, and it will stand for you, and light will shine upon your ways.

verses.rationale: Choose encouragement for the difficult exaltation phrase, with alternatives noted.
verses.before: When people are brought low, you will say, ‘Lift up!’ and he will save the one of lowered eyes.
verses.after: When people are brought low, you will say, ‘Lift them up!’ He will save those whose eyes are lowered.
verses.tsw_comparator: When people are brought low, you will say, ‘Lift up!’ and he will save the one of lowered eyes.

verses.rationale: Retain the consequential not-innocent reading and proposed benefit to another.
verses.before: He will deliver even one who is not innocent; he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”
verses.after: He will rescue even one who is not innocent; that person will be rescued through the cleanness of your hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will deliver even one who is not innocent; he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands.”

verses.rationale: Mark Job’s response to Eliphaz’s accusations.
verses.before: Then Job answered and said:
verses.after: Then Job answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Retain the pinned my hand and difficult complaint term, explaining alternatives in notes.
verses.before: “Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy despite my groaning.
verses.after: “Even today my complaint is defiant; my hand lies heavy over my groaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand is heavy despite my groaning.

verses.rationale: Keep the longing to locate God for a hearing.
verses.before: If only I knew where to find him, that I might come to his seat!
verses.after: If only I knew where to find him! I would come right to his dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: If only I knew where to find him, that I might come to his seat!

verses.rationale: Retain the legal preparation and speaking image.
verses.before: I would arrange my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.after: I would arrange my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would arrange my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.

verses.rationale: Keep the desire for an intelligible reply.
verses.before: I would know the words he would answer me and understand what he would say to me.
verses.after: I would learn the words of his answer and understand what he would say to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I would know the words he would answer me and understand what he would say to me.

verses.rationale: Preserve Job’s moment of confidence in being heard.
verses.before: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No; surely he would give attention to me.
verses.after: Would he oppose me with his great power? No—he would pay attention to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No; surely he would give attention to me.

verses.rationale: Keep the imagined hearing and release from judgment.
verses.before: There an upright person could argue with him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.
verses.after: There an upright person could argue with him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.
verses.tsw_comparator: There an upright person could argue with him, and I would be delivered forever from my judge.

verses.rationale: Retain the failed search and directional parallel.
verses.before: Look, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him;
verses.after: But I go forward, and he is not there; backward, and I cannot perceive him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I go forward, but he is not there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him;

verses.rationale: Keep all four directions without forcing a compass interpretation.
verses.before: to the left where he works, but I cannot look him; he turns to the right, but I cannot see him.
verses.after: To the left, where he works, I cannot behold him; he turns to the right, and I cannot see him.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the left where he works, but I cannot behold him; he turns to the right, but I cannot see him.

verses.rationale: Preserve knowledge of Job’s way and the refining comparison.
verses.before: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I will come out like gold.
verses.after: But he knows the way I take. When he tests me, I will come out like gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I will come out like gold.

verses.rationale: Keep the bodily path image as Job’s claim of fidelity.
verses.before: My foot has held fast to his step; I have kept his way and not turned aside.
verses.after: My feet have held to his steps; I have kept his way without turning aside.
verses.tsw_comparator: My foot has held fast to his step; I have kept his way and not turned aside.

verses.rationale: Choose allotted food while noting the possible own decree reading.
verses.before: I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my appointed food.
verses.after: I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured his words more than my allotted food.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my appointed food.

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult unity phrase and unopposed will.
verses.before: But he is one, and who can turn him? What his soul desires, that he does.
verses.after: But he is of one purpose—who can turn him back? Whatever he desires, he does.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he is one, and who can turn him? What his soul desires, that he does.

verses.rationale: Keep the threatening appointed portion and unspecified further acts.
verses.before: For he will complete what is appointed for me, and many such things are with him.
verses.after: He will complete what is appointed for me, and he has many such things in store.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he will complete what is appointed for me, and many such things are with him.

verses.rationale: Preserve renewed fear after the earlier confidence.
verses.before: So I am terrified before his face; when I consider it, I am afraid of him.
verses.after: That is why I am terrified before him; when I consider it, I am afraid of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I am terrified before his face; when I consider it, I am afraid of him.

verses.rationale: Keep the explicit divine cause of fear.
verses.before: God has made my heart faint, and the Almighty has terrified me,
verses.after: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
verses.tsw_comparator: God has made my heart faint, and the Almighty has terrified me,

verses.rationale: Choose silenced for the difficult destruction/silence verb, with the alternative reading noted.
verses.before: yet I am not silenced by the darkness or by the thick darkness that covers my face.”
verses.after: Yet I am not silenced by darkness, by the thick gloom that covers my face.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet I am not silenced by the darkness or by the thick darkness that covers my face.”

verses.rationale: Make judgment implicit in the context while noting the compressed wording.
verses.before: “Why are times not stored up by the Almighty? Why do people who know him not see his days?
verses.after: Why does the Almighty not appoint times for judgment? Why do those who know him never see his days?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Why are times not stored up by the Almighty? Why do those who know him not see his days?

verses.rationale: Keep concrete property theft and continued possession.
verses.before: People move boundary markers; they seize flocks and pasture them.
verses.after: People move boundary stones; they steal flocks and pasture them.
verses.tsw_comparator: People move boundary markers; they seize flocks and pasture them.

verses.rationale: Preserve the particular victims and livelihood animals.
verses.before: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow’s ox as a pledge.
verses.after: They drive away the orphan’s donkey and take the widow’s ox as a pledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow’s ox as a pledge.

verses.rationale: Keep forced exclusion and collective hiding.
verses.before: They turn the needy aside from the road; the poor of the land hide themselves together.
verses.after: They push the needy off the road; the poor of the land must hide together.
verses.tsw_comparator: They turn the needy aside from the road; the poor of the land hide themselves together.

verses.rationale: Clarify the shift to impoverished laborers while preserving the wild-donkey comparison.
verses.before: Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, seeking food; the wasteland provides food for them and for their children.
verses.after: Like wild donkeys in the wilderness, the poor go out to their work, searching for food. The desert supplies bread for their children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, seeking food; the wasteland provides food for them and for their children.

verses.rationale: Keep the poor working another’s land and the seasonal gleaning.
verses.before: In the field they harvest another’s fodder, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
verses.after: They reap fodder in the fields and glean late grapes in the wicked person’s vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the field they harvest another’s fodder, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.

verses.rationale: Preserve exposure without euphemism.
verses.before: They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
verses.after: They spend the night naked, without clothing, with no covering against the cold.
verses.tsw_comparator: They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.

verses.rationale: Keep the physical search for minimal refuge.
verses.before: They are wet with the rain of the mountains, and for lack of shelter they embrace the rock.
verses.after: Drenched by mountain storms, they cling to a rock for lack of shelter.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are wet with the rain of the mountains, and for lack of shelter they embrace the rock.

verses.rationale: Retain the nursing child’s seizure and the compressed pledge clause without inventing its object.
verses.before: They tear the fatherless from the breast, and they take a pledge against the poor.
verses.after: The orphan is snatched from the breast, and a pledge is taken from the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: They tear the fatherless from the breast, and they take a pledge against the poor.

verses.rationale: Keep the labor-and-deprivation contradiction.
verses.before: Naked, they go about without clothing; hungry, they carry sheaves.
verses.after: They go about naked, without clothing; hungry, they carry sheaves of grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Naked, they go about without clothing; hungry, they carry sheaves.

verses.rationale: Retain uncertain walls or rows and the workers’ denied drink.
verses.before: Between their walls they press oil; they tread winepresses, yet thirst.
verses.after: Between the walls they press oil; they tread winepresses, yet go thirsty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Between their walls they press oil; they tread winepresses, yet thirst.

verses.rationale: Keep the pointed claim of absent accountability, with alternative heedlessness reading noted.
verses.before: From the city the dying groan, and the life of the wounded cries out, yet God does not charge it as folly.
verses.after: People groan from the city; the wounded cry out for help. Yet God does not charge anyone with wrongdoing.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the city the dying groan, and the life of the wounded cries out, yet God does not charge it as folly.

verses.rationale: Preserve light as a moral and temporal image.
verses.before: These are among people who rebel against the light; they do not recognize its ways or remain in its paths.
verses.after: There are those who rebel against the light, who do not know its ways or remain in its paths.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are among those who rebel against the light; they do not recognize its ways or remain in its paths.

verses.rationale: Retain both times and targeted vulnerable people.
verses.before: At daylight the murderer rises; he kills the poor and needy, and in the night he becomes like a thief.
verses.after: The murderer rises at daylight and kills the poor and needy; at night he acts as a thief.
verses.tsw_comparator: At daylight the murderer rises; he kills the poor and needy, and in the night he becomes like a thief.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated seeing language and concealment.
verses.before: The eye of the adulterer waits for twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me,’ and he puts a covering on his face.
verses.after: The adulterer’s eye waits for twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me,’ and he covers his face.
verses.tsw_comparator: The eye of the adulterer waits for twilight, saying, ‘No eye will see me,’ and he puts a covering on his face.

verses.rationale: Preserve ancient housebreaking through walls and reversed daily activity.
verses.before: In darkness they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in. They do not know the light.
verses.after: In darkness they dig into houses; by day they shut themselves in. They do not know the light.
verses.tsw_comparator: In darkness they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in. They do not know the light.

verses.rationale: Keep the paradoxical reversed light and familiar terror.
verses.before: For morning is death-shadow to all of them, for they recognize the terrors of death-shadow.
verses.after: For all of them, morning is deep darkness; they are familiar with the terrors of deep shadow.
verses.tsw_comparator: For morning is death-shadow to all of them, for they recognize the terrors of death-shadow.

verses.rationale: Retain the abrupt shift and possible description or curse without adding a speaker. Retains the source shift from singular to plural rather than smoothing it away.
verses.before: Swift is he upon the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the land; he does not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
verses.after: He is swept swiftly along the water’s surface; their portion in the land is cursed. He no longer turns toward the vineyards.
verses.tsw_comparator: Swift is he upon the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the land; he does not turn toward the way of the vineyards.

verses.rationale: Keep the comparison and supplied parallel verb.
verses.before: Drought and heat steal away snow waters; so Sheol people who have sinned.
verses.after: Drought and heat snatch away snow water; Sheol does the same to those who have sinned.
verses.tsw_comparator: Drought and heat steal away snow waters; so Sheol those who have sinned.

verses.rationale: Preserve bodily origin, decay, and personified injustice.
verses.before: The womb forgets him; the worm finds him sweet. He is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
verses.after: The womb forgets him; worms feast on him. He is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: The womb forgets him; the worm finds him sweet. He is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.

verses.rationale: Keep the specified vulnerable women and predatory action.
verses.before: He devours the barren woman who does not give birth and does no good to the widow.
verses.after: He preys on the barren woman who has no child and does no good to the widow.
verses.tsw_comparator: He devours the barren woman who does not give birth and does no good to the widow.

verses.rationale: Choose divine agency while noting the uncertain subjects and verb.
verses.before: Yet God draws the mighty away by his power; he rises, and no one is sure of life.
verses.after: Yet God draws away the mighty by his power; he rises, and they have no assurance of life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet God draws the mighty away by his power; he rises, and no one is sure of life.

verses.rationale: Preserve permitted security alongside surveillance.
verses.before: He gives them security, and they lean upon it, but his eyes are upon their ways.
verses.after: He gives them security, and they rely on it; but his eyes are on their ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: He gives them security, and they lean upon it, but his eyes are upon their ways.

verses.rationale: Keep the shared mortality and harvest image rather than asserting a special mode of punishment.
verses.before: They are exalted a little while, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered like all others; they are cut off like the heads of grain.
verses.after: They are exalted a little while, then are gone. They are brought low and gathered in like everyone else, cut off like heads of grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are exalted a little while, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered like all others; they are cut off like the heads of grain.

verses.rationale: Preserve the closing challenge to rebut the argument.
verses.before: If it is not so, who will prove me a liar and make my word nothing?”
verses.after: If this is not so, who will prove me a liar and show that my words amount to nothing?”
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is not so, who will prove me a liar and make my word nothing?”

verses.rationale: Identify the brief third speech as Bildad’s.
verses.before: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.after: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:

verses.rationale: Keep divine rule, fear, and heavenly order together.
verses.before: “Dominion and dread are with him; he makes peace in his heights.
verses.after: “Dominion and dread belong to him; he makes peace in his heights.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Dominion and dread are with him; he makes peace in his heights.

verses.rationale: Retain the army and universal light questions.
verses.before: Is there any number to his armies? And upon whom does his light not rise?
verses.after: Can his troops be numbered? On whom does his light not rise?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is there any number to his armies? And upon whom does his light not rise?

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated argument about human purity.
verses.before: How then can a human be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
verses.after: How can a mortal be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
verses.tsw_comparator: How then can a human be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?

verses.rationale: Keep the comparison as a theological claim, not astronomy.
verses.before: Look, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes.
verses.after: Even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes.

verses.rationale: Retain the degrading description in Bildad’s voice.
verses.before: How much less a human, a maggot, and a son of man, a worm!”
verses.after: How much less a mortal, a maggot, a human being, a worm!”
verses.tsw_comparator: How much less a human, a maggot, and a son of man, a worm!”

verses.rationale: Preserve the manuscript’s speaker assignment for the whole chapter.
verses.before: Then Job answered and said:
verses.after: Then Job answered:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Job answered and said:

verses.rationale: Keep the sarcastic praise and weak arm image.
verses.before: “How you have helped one without power! How you have saved an arm without strength!
verses.after: “How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm without strength!
verses.tsw_comparator: “How you have helped one without power! How you have saved an arm without strength!

verses.rationale: Preserve sarcasm through parallel exclamations.
verses.before: How you have counseled one without wisdom and made sound wisdom abundantly known!
verses.after: What counsel you have given the unwise! What an abundance of sound wisdom you have made known!
verses.tsw_comparator: How you have counseled one without wisdom and made sound wisdom abundantly known!

verses.rationale: Keep the challenge to the source and audience of the speech.
verses.before: To whom have you declared words, and whose breath came out from you?
verses.after: To whom have you spoken these words? Whose breath has come out of you?
verses.tsw_comparator: To whom have you declared words, and whose breath came out from you?

verses.rationale: Retain the realm of the dead and cosmic depth.
verses.before: The shades tremble beneath the waters and their inhabitants.
verses.after: The shades tremble beneath the waters and their inhabitants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The shades tremble beneath the waters and their inhabitants.

verses.rationale: Preserve both underworld terms and exposure.
verses.before: Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.
verses.after: Sheol lies naked before him; Abaddon has no covering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.

verses.rationale: Keep the poetic cosmic image without converting it into a modern scientific claim.
verses.before: He stretches out the north over emptiness; he hangs the earth upon nothing.
verses.after: He stretches the north over emptiness and hangs the earth on nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stretches out the north over emptiness; he hangs the earth upon nothing.

verses.rationale: Retain the contained-water wonder.
verses.before: He binds up waters in his clouds, and the cloud does not burst beneath them.
verses.after: He binds up water in his clouds, yet the cloud does not split beneath it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He binds up waters in his clouds, and the cloud does not burst beneath them.

verses.rationale: Choose throne while noting the possible full-moon reading.
verses.before: He covers the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it.
verses.after: He covers the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He covers the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it.

verses.rationale: Keep the horizon-like boundary image.
verses.before: He inscribed a circle upon the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.
verses.after: He draws a circle on the surface of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness.
verses.tsw_comparator: He inscribed a circle upon the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.

verses.rationale: Preserve cosmic pillars and personification.
verses.before: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
verses.after: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his rebuke.

verses.rationale: Keep the mythic combat imagery and note stirred as an alternative verb sense.
verses.before: By his power he stilled the sea, and by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
verses.after: By his power he stilled the Sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
verses.tsw_comparator: By his power he stilled the sea, and by his understanding he shattered Rahab.

verses.rationale: Preserve breath, hand, and the ancient serpent image.
verses.before: By his breath the heavens became fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
verses.after: By his breath the heavens became clear; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
verses.tsw_comparator: By his breath the heavens became fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.

verses.rationale: Follow plural ways and mighty deeds and retain the whisper/thunder contrast.
verses.before: Look, these are only the edges of his ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear of him! But the thunder of his power—who can understand?”
verses.after: These are only the edges of his ways; how faint a whisper we hear of him! Who can understand the thunder of his mighty deeds?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, these are only the edges of his ways, and what a whisper of a word we hear of him! But the thunder of his power—who can understand?”
